title: Lesson 1: what, how, where
meta_description: Every placement in your chart has three parts. Learn these and you can read any chart.
summary: Every placement in your chart has three parts. Learn these and you can read any chart.
body_md:
Every placement in your chart has three parts. Learn these and you can read any chart.

The planet is what: the part of you that acts. The Sun is your self, the Moon your mind, Mars your drive (Brihat Jataka 2.1).

The sign is how: the way it acts. Fire signs act boldly, earth signs steadily, air signs think and connect, water signs feel and protect (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, on the signs).

The house is where: the area of life. The 1st house is you, the 4th your home, the 7th your partner, the 10th your career.

Put it together. Mars in Leo in the 10th house: your drive leads, with pride, in your career.

Try it with your Moon. Which sign, which house? Write your sentence in the comments.

Next lesson: the Sun

In Jyotish the Sun is your self. Varahamihira calls it the soul (Brihat Jataka 2.1). It shows your confidence and purpose, your father and the people in charge of you, and your health and energy.

In Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, the Sun is strongest in Aries (exalted), at home in Leo (its own sign) and weakest in Libra (debilitated).

By house, it does best in the 10th, the house of career. Parashara gives the Sun full strength there, so a 10th house Sun tends to live a visible life.

The Upanishads say of the Self: "That is the pure light of all lights" (Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.9). In your chart, the Sun stands for that light.

In Jyotish each graha (Sanskrit for "the one who grabs") is a character in your life's story. The Moon is the mother: your mind. Varahamihira calls it the mind of Time (Brihat Jataka 2.1). It shows how you feel and react, your mother and your home, and how you rest.

In Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, the Moon is strongest in Taurus (exalted), at home in Cancer (its own sign) and weakest in Scorpio (debilitated).

Its phase matters too. A bright, growing Moon is gentle and strong; a dark, fading Moon is weaker. So check whether you were born under a growing or a fading Moon.

The Mahabharata explains the phases with a story. The 27 stars were Daksha's daughters, all married to the Moon. The Moon loved Rohini most, so Daksha cursed him to waste away. The curse was softened, and ever since the Moon fades and grows again (Shalya Parva).

Try it with your Moon. Which sign is it in, and was it bright or dark? Tell me in the comments.

title: Your 12th house is your rest budget
h1: Your 12th house is your rest budget
meta_description: Most people fear the 12th house: loss, bills, hospitals. Here is a more useful way to read it. The 12th house shows what you have to spend, give up or…
summary: Most people fear the 12th house: loss, bills, hospitals. Here is a more useful way to read it. The 12th house shows what you have to spend, give up or switch off from, so you can keep going.
body_md:
Most people fear the 12th house: loss, bills, hospitals. Here is a more useful way to read it. The 12th house shows what you have to spend, give up or switch off from, so you can keep going.

For one person it's sleep: every short night costs them the next day. For another it's distance: a life in a new city or country, and the price is missing family dinners and festivals back home. For another it's quiet time: a weekend offline, a prayer hour, giving to a cause.

Parashara calls the 12th vyaya, the house of spending (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra), and the old texts give it sleep as well. That pairing makes sense in city life. When you don't rest, you pay for it anyway: the late-night takeout, the cancelled plans, the clinic visit, the bad decision made tired.

Sutra: "What you won't spend on rest, you will spend on recovery"

A strong 12th house often makes you good at letting go: switching off, travelling, living abroad, healing work, helping people quietly.

Practical remedy: open your bank app and look at the last three months. Circle every charge that came from being tired, and add it up. Then put two hours of real rest in your calendar this week, before anything else gets booked.

body_md:

Sade Sati is the stretch when it passes through three signs in a row: the one before your Moon sign, your Moon sign, and the one after. Three signs, about seven and a half years. People call it bad luck. It works more like an audit at work. Saturn checks what you built and how you built it. Things built on shortcuts get tested. Things built on steady effort usually hold.

For one person it's a job they stayed in out of fear, which finally stops working. For another it's health habits running on credit: years of late nights and skipped meals that start sending the bill. For another it's a relationship on autopilot, which now needs real attention.

Sutra: "Saturn takes away what you were only holding out of habit"

Where you are now:

Pisces Moon: the middle and heaviest part, until June 2027  
Aries Moon: just started, running to 2032

What Saturn rewards: routine, patience, honest work, and care for elders and for the people who work for you

Practical remedy: write down three things you keep doing only out of habit, and drop one this month. Then give every Saturday one hour of real work on the thing you keep putting off. Saturday is Saturn's day, and Saturn respects people who show up.

title: The 8th house: other people's money
meta_description: The 8th house scares people: death, accidents, scandal. Parashara reads longevity from it (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra), which is where the scary…
summary: The 8th house scares people: death, accidents, scandal. Parashara reads longevity from it (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra), which is where the scary reputation comes from. In everyday life it shows the parts of your life that depend on other people's money and other people's decisions.
body_md:
The 8th house scares people: death, accidents, scandal. Parashara reads longevity from it (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra), which is where the scary reputation comes from. In everyday life it shows the parts of your life that depend on other people's money and other people's decisions.

For one person it's a spouse's income: when their job changes, your plans change too. For another it's shared family property: the house back home that five relatives have a say in. For another it's the paperwork nobody enjoys: insurance, taxes, a loan you co-signed, a business partner's debt.

Here is why the 8th covers your partner's money. The 7th house is your partner. The 2nd house is money. Count your partner's house as their 1st, and their 2nd house lands on your 8th. Astrologers call this bhavat bhavam, house from house, and use it all the time.

Sutra: "You can't control the 8th house. You can prepare for it"

A strong 8th house makes people calm when things go wrong. Surgeons, researchers, investigators, insurance and tax people, the cousin everyone calls in a crisis.

Practical remedy: make one folder your family could open if you were unreachable for a month: bank accounts, insurance policies, important documents, and who to call for what. Tell one person where it is. Update it every Diwali, along with the cleaning.
ask_question: What does my 8th house hold?

title: Four houses in your chart get better with age
h1: Four houses in your chart get better with age
meta_description: The 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses are called upachaya, which means "increase" (Varahamihira, Brihat Jataka, chapter 1). Whatever sits in these houses…
summary: The 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses are called upachaya, which means "increase" (Varahamihira, Brihat Jataka, chapter 1). Whatever sits in these houses tends to start slow and grow with effort.
body_md:
The 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses are called upachaya, which means "increase" (Varahamihira, Brihat Jataka, chapter 1). Whatever sits in these houses tends to start slow and grow with effort.

What each one covers in modern life:  
3rd: your courage and your own hustle (the side project, the cold email, the first video you post)  
6th: your daily grind (the job you show up to, the gym routine, how you handle a difficult coworker)  
10th: your career (your title, your reputation at work, what people know you for)  
11th: your income and network (raises, clients, the friend who refers you for a job)

This is why the old texts are kind to "hard" grahas here (graha is Sanskrit for "the one who grabs": the nine forces in your chart). Saturn, the auditor, and Mars, the soldier, usually bring pressure. In the 3rd, 6th or 11th, that pressure turns into stamina. Think of a tough coach: unpleasant when you're 22, the reason you're good at 35.

Sutra: "Some parts of your chart are meant to start rough"

Practical remedy: find out which of these four houses has a graha in your chart. If life in that area felt slow in your twenties, that was the warm-up. Pick one habit that feeds it (one networking message a week for the 11th, one fixed workout routine for the 6th) and give it three honest years before you judge it.
ask_question: Which of my upachaya houses is busy, and what gets better with age for me?

title: Your dasha: the chapter you're in
h1: Your dasha: the chapter you're in
meta_description: Most people check the daily stuff: Mercury walking backward, the Moon's sign, what Saturn is doing this month. Underneath that runs a bigger clock.…
summary: Most people check the daily stuff: Mercury walking backward, the Moon's sign, what Saturn is doing this month. Underneath that runs a bigger clock. body_md:
Most people check the daily stuff: Mercury walking backward, the Moon's sign, what Saturn is doing this month. Underneath that runs a bigger clock. Jyotish splits your life into periods called dashas (Sanskrit for "stage of life"), and each one is run by a single graha (Sanskrit for "the one who grabs": the nine characters in your chart). In Parashara's main system, Vimshottari ("the 120"), the full cycle runs 120 years, and each graha gets its own stretch, from 6 years for the Sun to 20 for Venus (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra).

The graha whose period you're in is the main character of those years. It sets the theme. Where that graha sits in your chart shows which part of life the theme plays out in.

For one person it's a Saturn period, the auditor's chapter: 19 years of building slowly, a career that rewards patience more than talent  
For another it's a Rahu period, the magician's chapter: 18 years of wanting more, new cities, new industries, big swings  
For another it's a Jupiter period, the teacher's chapter: 16 years of teachers, study, children and a wider circle

A transit is a few weeks or months of weather inside that chapter. A rainy week in a good chapter is still a good chapter. A sunny week in a hard chapter doesn't change the plot.

Sutra: "Read the chapter before you blame the weather"

Practical remedy: find out which graha's period you're in, and which house that graha sits in. Write one line: "These years are about ___". Check every big decision against that line, and let today's horoscope wait.
ask_question: Which dasha am I in, and what is this chapter about?

body_md:
Your chart has twelve houses, called bhavas in Sanskrit, and each one holds a part of your life. Parashara lists wealth, grain and family under the 2nd (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 11.3), and astrologers read your speech there too: the same mouth that eats also talks. Money, speech, family and food. It sounds like a random mix until you watch how real people live.

For one person it's the family dinner table: the way money was talked about there becomes the way they handle it for life  
For another it's speech at work: the person who can say "this is my rate" without apologising usually earns more  
For another it's food: the daily takeout and coffee runs that quietly decide whether anything is left to save

The old astrologers put these under one house because they saw one system. What goes into your mouth, and what comes out of it, shapes what you keep. A strong 2nd house often gives a voice people trust, a steady saver, and a family that stays close around meals.

Sutra: "What you say about money becomes what you do with it"

Practical remedy: for one week, catch every sentence you say about money ("I'm bad with money", "we can never afford it"). Swap one for a plain fact ("I have $400 left this month"). Cook at home three nights, and write down what you saved.
ask_question: What does my 2nd house say about my savings and my words?

body_md:
Picture someone walking home who looks back, sees a person drowning, changes path and goes to save them. That's a graha walking backward. A graha (Sanskrit for "the one who grabs") is one of the nine characters in your chart, and Sanskrit calls one that walks backward vakri, "the crooked one". It turns around and goes back for what was missed.

Nothing in the sky really reverses. From Earth, a graha seems to walk backward when we overtake it, or it overtakes us, and that happens when it's at its closest to us. Parashara gives a graha walking backward full strength of motion (Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, on strength). In real life that strength often shows up as going back and doing it better.

Right now three are walking backward: the messenger (Mercury) and the lover (Venus) until 13 November, and the auditor (Saturn) until 10 December. Some people are born with one or more of them that way.

For one person it's the messenger walking backward: they rewrite every email and end up the best editor in the office  
For another it's the lover walking backward: love and money choices get a second look, and the second choice is the one that lasts  
For another it's the auditor walking backward: old duties come back to be finished properly, often later in life

Sutra: "Some gifts arrive as second drafts"

Practical remedy: find out if any graha in your chart walks backward. In that part of life, stop expecting to get it right the first time. Build in a review: sleep on the email, wait a week on the purchase, look at the plan again in a month.

Food: the body you feed  
Breath: your energy and drive  
Mind: your feelings and moods  
Knowing: your judgment and understanding  
Joy: the deepest layer

Later teachers called these the five koshas, "sheaths", one inside the next.

In your chart, each layer has a graha (Sanskrit for "the one who grabs") looking after it. This is Sutram's teaching map, built from the classical meanings of each one:  
Body: your Ascendant, the sign rising when you were born  
Breath: the Sun, the king, for vitality, and Mars, the soldier, for drive  
Mind: the Moon, the mother  
Knowing: Mercury, the messenger, and Jupiter, the teacher  
Joy: Venus, the lover, and Jupiter again

In real life it works like a checklist. Tired all week? Start with the body: sleep, food, a walk. Can't get going? The breath layer: morning light and movement. Can't switch off? The mind layer: a routine, a call home.

Bhrigu's last answer was joy: "From joy all beings are born, by joy they live, into joy they return" (Taittiriya Upanishad 3.6). Jyotish still carries his name too: the Bhrigu Samhita and Bhrigu Nandi Nadi are named for a sage Bhrigu.

Your birth chart works the same way. Each graha (Sanskrit for "the one who grabs") plays two parts at once: a part of you, and a person in your life.  
The Sun, the king: your soul and your father  
The Moon, the mother: your mind and your mother  
Mars, the soldier: your courage and your brothers  
Venus, the lover: your desire and your partner

Varahamihira sets out the grahas as one person, Kalapurusha, the Person of Time: soul, mind, strength, speech, knowledge, desire and sorrow (Brihat Jataka 2.1). Each house is a bhava, a "state of being": the 4th is your mother and your peace, the 7th your partner and your other half, the 10th your boss and your work.

In real life, the friend who always pushes you is your own Mars, out loud. The boss who checks every line is your own Saturn, the auditor. In the film, the projections fight back when the dream starts to change. In life, the hard people often show up just when a graha in you is changing.

Try this: think of the hardest person in your life right now and find their graha (father: Sun, mother: Moon, partner: Venus, boss: your 10th house). Treat that person a little better this week. The old remedies work the same way: honour your father for the Sun, care for your mother for the Moon.

Jupiter is the teacher: what you learned, your faith, your mentors, your savings. Ketu is the monk: what you outgrew, what you know without being taught, and the art of letting go.

Rule 1, same room. When two grahas sit in the same sign, they share a room and their stories mix. In Nadi this is the strongest link there is.

Rule 2, who walks in front. Inside the room, count the degrees. The graha with more degrees walks in front, and the one behind takes on the leader's nature.

Monk in front: the teacher becomes a monk. You stop following advice you were given and trust what you've lived. A mentor steps back, savings get given away, faith goes quiet and personal.

Teacher in front: the monk becomes a teacher. What you went through quietly becomes what you can teach, like the burnout survivor who starts coaching or the quiet meditator who opens a class.

Right now Jupiter and Ketu share Leo. From 31 October to 11 November the monk has more degrees, so the teacher turns monk. From 11 November to 5 December the teacher walks in front, so the monk turns teacher.

Sutra: "Let go first, then teach what's left"

The line comes from the Emerald Tablet, an Arabic text from about 800 CE credited to Hermes and read in Latin by 1151: "That which is above is like to that which is below." India said it too. Charaka writes "puruṣo'yaṃ lokasammitaḥ", a person is a measure of the world (Charaka Samhita, Sharira 5.3). In Jyotish, Parashara reads the twelve signs as the body of Time, and Varahamihira read the same sky for whole countries: rain, harvests, famine and war.

So we tested it. Right now Jupiter, the teacher, meets Ketu, the monk, in Leo, the king's palace (graha is Sanskrit for "the one who grabs"). Our engine checked every day since 1600. It happened only six times before: 1635, 1672, 1766, 1802, 1896 and 1932.

October 1635, almost this exact sky: Massachusetts banished a preacher, Roger Williams, for his beliefs. He founded Rhode Island on freedom of conscience  
June 1672, Saturn in Pisces like now: France invaded the Dutch Republic. The Dutch still call 1672 the disaster year  
August 1896, the same degree as this November: a man took Zanzibar's palace without approval, and the war that followed lasted about 38 minutes. Famine and plague hit India  
Autumn 1932: Gandhi fasted in prison until the Poona Pact, famine spread in Ukraine, the Depression hit bottom and America changed leader

What repeats: conscience against power, the palace contested, sudden strikes, and hardship that gives way to new freedoms.

What to watch, November to January: people of conscience stepping out, thrones tested, fights that flare fast (especially 12 to 16 November, when Mars joins), and food and money worries in places. These are rhymes to watch for; people still choose what they do with them.

So within: stand by what you've lived, don't take a seat you weren't offered, pick short clean fights, keep a small reserve this winter

Sutra: "When the sky rhymes, history rhymes"
